newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed on Wednesday with the short end out of favour, but prices bid well up in longer maturities as investors looked for value, dealers said.

Relief in world asset markets over comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday widely taken to indicate U.S. interest rates would remain on hold, saw yields falling and the curve flattening through the session.
"The flattening is the story of the day," one trader said. "Not unusual when we get an upmove -- people are definitely looking for value at the long end."
Buying interest was particularly focused in 30-year paper, a broker said, with some good business seen from Dutch domestic investors in otherwise moderate cash volume.
But Guilders did underperform Bunds across the curve, particularly at the very long end where buyers were preferring the new, strippable Bund issue, he added.
"There was a little panic and when there is, people tend to go for Germany."
Traders looking for technical signals were left guessing as the September Bund contract took off in an early rally to a contract high only to slip back later.
Chartists said they were now eyeing all-time highs above 104.00, with some warning failure at this hurdle could be the start of a big, sustained downmove.
New impetus would need to come from the U.S., one said, where Greenspan is presenting the second round of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate.
He had stuck to the same prepared remarks as Tuesday, but the question and answer session was be closely watched.
